clue.text: Top men added words about staying

indicators.note: about means the postscript letters go around the word for staying, one at each end

parts.note: words added at the end of a letter are a postscript, abbreviated PS
someone staying somewhere is resident there

explanation.surface: Senior figures tacked on remarks about remaining where they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Presidents are the heads of states or organisations, the people at the very top.

clue.text: Pity the young woman staying with her mother-in-law!

definitions.meaning: an old word for compassion, surviving in ruthless

definitions.text: the young woman staying with her mother-in-law!
definitions.meaning: the biblical widow who stayed with her mother-in-law Naomi, saying 'whither thou goest, I will go'

explanation.surface: Sympathy for a young wife stuck living with her husband's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Compassion is the old meaning, still found in ruthless; the biblical book tells of the Moabite widow loyal to Naomi.

clue.text: Boys, on rising, will grab almost any footwear

indicators.note: will grab means the reversed word for boys holds the shortened word inside it
in a down clue rising means the word for boys is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: lads are boys

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped from any

explanation.surface: Lads who get up will grab whatever shoes come to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on rising' turns LADS into SDAL; 'almost' makes AN from ANY, and SDAL 'will grab' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandal is an open shoe held on with straps, a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Far from reserved

explanation.surface: Anything but shy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a long way off in space and cool, aloof behaviour.

clue.text: Artless if an irregularity is discovered

indicators.note: an irregularity signals that the letters of 'if an' are put in a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: Unsophisticated, if some anomaly comes to light.
explanation.definitionFit: Naif, a form of naive, describes someone innocent and unaffected.

clue.text: Peace subsequently broken by the French

indicators.note: broken by means the word for subsequently is split open and the French article put inside

parts.note: since can mean subsequently, as in 'he has since left'
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Calm later shattered by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Silence is the absence of noise, a peaceful quiet.

clue.text: A forecaster must look to the skies

definitions.text: A forecaster must look to the skies

parts.words: A forecaster must look to the skies
parts.note: the surface suggests a weather forecaster scanning the clouds, but the prophet meant reads the future in the stars and planets

explanation.definitionFit: Such a person casts horoscopes from planetary positions, predicting events from the heavens.

clue.text: Robin's role as a father?

parts.note: the outlaw of Sherwood Forest was Robin Hood, so a father's role is pictured as being a mother or father combined with his surname

explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood is the legendary English outlaw; the clue joins his surname to the word for a mother or father.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being a mother or father is the role a father plays.

clue.text: Mount, as so ordered

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of 'as so' are arranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A mountain is named, its letters put in order as so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' is a noun for a mountain, not a verb: Ossa is a mountain in Greece, famous from the myth of piling Pelion on Ossa.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is a Greek peak, so it is a mountain, or mount in the poetic sense.

clue.text: A good man — and yet organising a hold-up!

parts.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST
taken as written
yet and still both mean nevertheless

explanation.surface: A virtuous fellow nonetheless masterminds a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold-up' suggests a robbery, but here it is a stoppage of traffic or progress; 'organising' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A hold-up in traffic brings everything to a halt, a complete stop.

clue.text: Come out for oriental combine

parts.note: oriental means eastern, abbreviated E
to combine two things is to merge them

explanation.surface: An invitation to step out for an eastern harvester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combine' reads as a farm machine (a combine harvester) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to appear from hiding, to step forth into view.

clue.text: Stick around a trainee using the phone

indicators.note: around means the word for stick wraps itself about the next two pieces

parts.note: to stick to something is to cling to it
a trainee driver is a learner, shown by the L-plate, so L

explanation.surface: A cane is waved around a novice who is busy on the telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a noun for a cane but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ringing a friend is placing a phone call to them.

clue.text: The opposition may be set against nurses

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
someone who nurses a patient tends them, so tenders

explanation.surface: Rivals may be lined up against the nursing staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Contenders are rivals competing against one another, the competition.

clue.text: Use of wood not all will find inept

parts.note: lumber is timber, sawn wood
some means a part rather than all

explanation.surface: Working with timber is something only part of the workforce does well.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbersome is an old variant of cumbersome, meaning clumsy and awkward.

clue.text: Feel around for g-string

parts.note: rope is thick string or cord

explanation.surface: Fumbling around for a skimpy piece of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'g-string' suggests skimpy underwear, but it is the letter G followed by a word for cord.
explanation.definitionFit: To grope is to search blindly by touch, fumbling with the hands.

clue.text: Mark obstruction in red

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
let is an old word for a hindrance, kept in the phrase 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A blemish on a barrier painted crimson.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a vivid shade of the colour, bright crimson.

clue.text: The skinhead and heel are inadequate

indicators.note: head means just the first letter of skin is taken

parts.note: a ship heels when it leans over; cant means to tilt in the same way

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed thug and a scoundrel are not up to much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' and 'heel' read as a thug and a cad, but 'head' takes S from 'skin' and 'heel' means tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely enough, insufficient in amount.

clue.text: React badly when there's suspicion

indicators.note: badly means the letters of react are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Respond poorly when someone is under suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspicion' here means a tiny hint, as in a suspicion of garlic.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is a very small amount, just a hint or touch of something.

clue.text: Unfeeling Greek character — a medico

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
a medico is a doctor, who may hold the MB, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted Greek who happens to be a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb means without sensation, deadened to touch or emotion.

clue.text: A private American ring for money-changing

parts.note: a GI is a private soldier in the US army
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A US soldier wears a ring while swapping currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Agio is the premium or fee charged when exchanging one currency for another.

clue.text: Weary of being told to go around quietly

indicators.note: around means the word for told to go encloses the letter for quietly

parts.note: someone told to go somewhere is sent there
p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: Tired of being ordered to tiptoe around.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone spent has used up all their energy, exhausted.

clue.text: Extensive period of imprisonment

parts.note: the word for a continuous expanse of time is also slang for a long prison sentence

explanation.definitionFit: In slang a long prison term is called doing time for an unbroken length of years.

clue.text: Trying time — a real pain

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: A difficult period that is genuinely painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' looks like difficult, as in a trying time, but means sampling food or drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasting a dish is trying it out, sampling its flavour.

clue.text: A recluse turning in before the time required

indicators.note: turning means the hidden letters are read backwards, right to left
in means the answer lies inside the run of letters across the time required

explanation.surface: A hermit turns up ahead of the appointed hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is a link word. It is tempting to build ERE (before) around a turned TIME, which also works, but the setter hid the word backwards across the closing words.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, especially a religious one living in solitude.

clue.text: Got less exercise and maybe rated about it

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters of rated go around the letters for exercise
maybe signals that the letters of rated may be rearranged

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone did less exercise and was perhaps graded accordingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' shuffles RATED into TARED, which goes 'about' PE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tapered became narrower or diminished, gradually reducing.

clue.text: One of two or possibly three going about one

indicators.note: going about means the jumbled letters of three surround the letter for one
possibly signals that the letters of three can be rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Two or maybe three people going around a single person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns THREE into ETHER, which goes about I.
explanation.definitionFit: The word picks out one or other of a pair, whichever of two options.

clue.text: After a party prudent medication is called for!

indicators.note: After places the word for prudent behind the word for a party

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
sage means wise or prudent

explanation.surface: Following a celebration, sensible people reach for something to ease the hangover.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosage is the measured amount of a drug to be taken, the prescribed dose.

clue.text: The beast advocates accommodating none

indicators.note: accommodating means the word for advocates holds the letter for none

parts.note: barristers collectively are the Bar
O looks like zero, so none

explanation.surface: The lawyers make room for no animals at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a wild pig, a beast of the forest.

clue.text: A joint in the neck needing support sometimes

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the run of letters across neck needing

explanation.surface: A joint in the neck may need some support from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge between thigh and shin, a joint of the leg.

clue.text: Deceived the worker and so assumed control

parts.note: to be taken in is to be deceived, so took in means deceived
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: Someone tricked the labourer and seized command.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking something in hand means taking charge of it, managing it.

clue.text: Sheep drives

definitions.meaning: forces or thrusts hard, as in pushing a point home

explanation.surface: Livestock that pushes forward.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the plural of a male sheep; the verb means forcing in hard, like a ram-raider.

clue.text: A simple plot

parts.note: simple is an old name for a medicinal plant, so a plot of simples is a bed where such plants are grown; the surface suggests an uncomplicated storyline

explanation.definitionFit: Simples are medicinal plants, and the plot is a patch of ground where they grow.
